findings.where: Whole tile, most of all the hero (desktop-01, phone-01): no photograph or film of Mark, and no slot that shows how one would sit on the blueprint sheet
findings.fault: Mark is never seen. All the hero's imagery is white linework of the logo's arches. Nothing on the tile shows how a photograph of Mark, or a photo from his projects (the 'refresh the images' rule), would sit on a diazo-blue grid sheet drawn in white lines. The brief's client value 3 ('the man himself') and value 8 (video welcome) go unanswered, so this direction never shows whether it can hold him.
findings.who_objects: The brief says every tile must answer each client value, so the founder and Mark would object: they can't judge whether this direction can show the person who is the brand. A development-bank officer on a first visit would object too, because first-visit trust item 1 asks for a real named person with a real photo of his face, and here there is only a name over an engineering drawing.

findings.where: Hero name block: the role lines under 'MARK M. MOSELEY' ('INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR / LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS'), with the circled 'A' section marker beside the name and the 'DRAWING MMM-GA-001 / SCALE NTS' title-block cells (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: The one line that says who Mark is shares a style and a block with drawing-office captions. By similarity and proximity, 'Infrastructure advisor' reads as one more label on the drawing, and is no longer his role. 'NTS' appears three times on the first screen. Together with the drawing number and the 'A' callout, the chrome makes the hero read as an engineering firm's general-arrangement sheet. It does not read as one experienced legal and PPP advisor speaking for himself.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff looking for a PPP or legal infrastructure advisor would object: in the 5-second test they could take him for an engineering design consultant, and his role is buried in jargon they don't need. Mark would object too. His brand sheet (§5) asks for a personal, approachable advisor's voice, not a firm's.

findings.where: Article specimen ('The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law', desktop-02 to desktop-03, phone-02): body text, pull quote and related-item box set straight over the full blueprint grid
findings.fault: On the article page, a page meant for reading, the grid of major and minor lines runs through every line of prose with no quieter reading field. The look built for a one-moment hero carries over unchanged to long reading. A post that Angélique adds will be a long block of text on top of graph paper.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's articles would object, because the lines crossing the text make long reading busy and tiring. Mark has said busyness is the thing he dislikes. The founder would object because the brief asks the identity to serve article pages in Read mode and to hold up when a lay editor adds a post (value 9).

findings.where: Hero drawing, the thin S-curve rising from the ground line to the right of the third arch (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: A single unexplained line climbs off the right end of the section. It isn't dimensioned, labelled or part of the logo, so by continuity it reads as a stray stroke or an unfinished element. On a sheet where every other line is a deliberate, labelled drawing convention, it stands out.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor's eye goes to the one line that doesn't fit, which pulls it away from the name and the action. Mark would object too: the logo must stay as it is and must not be redrawn, and this line looks like something added onto it.
